title: BBQ Chicken Bowls
shortDescription: Built bowls, big flavor, one line
subtitle: Built bowls, big flavor, one line
description: Built bowls, big flavor, one line. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Bring to a boil with 4½ cups water and 1 tsp salt, then cover and simmer on low 18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes off heat, fluff, and hold covered in a 200°F oven.

steps.title: Grill the chicken thighs
steps.instruction: Toss chicken thighs with 1 tbsp oil and the BBQ rub. Grill over medium-high 5–7 minutes per side until char marks show and thickest part reads 165°F. Rest 5 minutes; slice into strips.

steps.title: Warm the BBQ sauce
steps.instruction: Warm BBQ sauce in a small pot over low heat — do not boil or sugars scorch. Keep a ladle on the line.

steps.title: Char the corn and dress the slaw
steps.instruction: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add corn in an even layer and leave it 3–4 minutes until kernels blister and brown in spots; stir, season with a pinch of salt, and cook 2 minutes more. Toss coleslaw mix with mayonnaise, vinegar, and the remaining salt until just coated.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.instruction: Base of rice, sliced BBQ chicken, corn, and a pile of coleslaw on top for crunch. Drizzle extra sauce on the side. BBQ Chicken Bowls move fastest when hot and cold components are in separate pans.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Set rice or grain in the first pan, main in the second, crunchy toppings last so textures stay distinct.
Put hot components closest to the crew, cold crunch at the far end of the line.
Line up BBQ Chicken Bowls on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Built bowls, big flavor, one line. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).

adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free rub or build your own from confirmed gluten-free spices.
